candidates.name: Listeria monocytogenes meningitis
support_spans: cerebrospinal fluid analysis: Clear fluid, normal glucose level, increased protein level, 108 cells/mL (95% neutrophils)
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and cerebrospinal fluid analysis are consistent with Listeria monocytogenes meningitis, which can cause impaired extraocular movement, tetraparesis, and neck stiffness.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because Listeria monocytogenes meningitis is a rare cause of meningitis, especially in immunocompetent patients.

candidates.name: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML)
support_spans: 10-year history of treatment with various medications (glatiramer acetate, interferon beta, fingolimod, natalizumab, and most recently dimethyl fumarate for 3 years)
candidates.why: The patient's long history of immunosuppressive treatment increases the risk of PML, which can cause impaired extraocular movement, tetraparesis, and cognitive decline.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because PML is a rare but serious complication of immunosuppressive therapy.

candidates.name: Brainstem encephalitis
support_spans: T2 fluid-attenuated inversion recovery showed hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum with slight contrast enhancement
candidates.why: The patient's MRI findings are consistent with brainstem encephalitis, which can cause impaired extraocular movement, tetraparesis, and neck stiffness.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because brainstem encephalitis is a rare and potentially life-threatening condition that requires prompt diagnosis and treatment.

key_evidence_spans: mild sinking of the right leg
cerebrospinal fluid analysis: Clear fluid, normal glucose level, increased protein level, 108 cells/mL (95% neutrophils)

unexplained_specific_evidence: Moderate tetraparesis, headache, fever, and neck stiffness

selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, such as fever, neck stiffness, and positive cerebrospinal fluid culture, strongly support CNS infection. While brainstem encephalitis is also a possibility due to the hyperintense lesion in the brainstem, the positive cerebrospinal fluid culture points more towards a CNS infection.
